newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seen tendering for 54,000T corn, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seen tendering for 54,000T corn, soybeans.

text.p: Taiwan importers could hold one tender for 54,000 tonnes of corn and soybeans as early as next week, local traders said on Friday.
Hui Shung Group may place a tender within two weeks for a combined shipment totaling 54,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and soybeans, one trader said.
Details of the planned shipment were not immediately available, but traders expect it would be scheduled for March delivery.
Taiwan buyers in general want to stay close to each other's prices to prevent large comparitive gaps between companies' import costs, he added.
Taiwan's soymeal price for Taipei delivery was T$9.7 to T$9.8 a kg on Friday, the same as a week earlier.
Corn powder was also priced unchanged at between T$6.95 to T$7 a kg for Taipei delivery.

Freight rates on the Pacific Northwest to Taiwan route were indicated at about US$11.50 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico at between US$20.50 and US$21.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.

The Taiwan Flour Mills Association bought two shipments totalling 72,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat on December 4 and is likely to stay out of the market next week, association official Lu Wei-chih said on Friday.
Weekly local flour prices listed on Monday ranged between T$14.55 to T$15.68 kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier.
